==Errors==
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=4m49s|text=4:49}} [[Ingtar]] was in command, ''not'' [[Rand]]. Rand was Ingtar's second, not the other way around.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=6m34s|text=6:34}} The animation implies that [[Mat]] and [[Perrin]] were with Rand as he arrived in [[Cairhien]], but they were still days behind, with [[Ingtar]] and the other [[Shienar|Shienarans]] (and [[Verin]] at some point).
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=6m58s|text=6:58}} [[Rand]] met [[Thom]] ''before'' encountering the [[Trollocs]] in the [[Foregate]]. That's why [[Loial]] was with Rand when they encountered the Trollocs - after meeting Thom, Rand returned to his inn and brought Loial to meet Thom. Even this second meeting occurred ''before'' Loial and Rand were pursued by Trollocs and fled into the [[Guild of Illuminators|Illuminators']] compound.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=7m03s|text=7:03}} [[Rand]] discovered the [[Horn of Valere|Horn]] had been retaken by [[Fain]] when he returned to his inn after escaping the [[Guild of Illuminators|Illuminators']] compound, not while he was with [[Thom]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=8m01s|text=8:01}} It would be "'''''a''''' nearby Stedding", not "nearby Stedding". Also, while it is understood that the animation is merely simplifying things, the animation as presented implies [[Rand|Rand's]] party traveled some distance to the west - even to [[Andor]] - to reach Stedding [[Tsofu]], but Tsofu is actually slightly to the east of their origin (the city of [[Cairhien]]).
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=8m17s|text=8:17}} "Losing four months to their normal journey" is an odd and misleading phrase. About four months passed during the [[Portal Stone]] transit, but obviously a normal journey would not have been four months quicker. They probably only lost a month or two.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=9m25s|text=9:25}} [[Rand|Rand's]] party did ''not'' try to take [[Egwene]] with them. Rand saw Egwene and ''wanted'' to take her, but there was no opportunity to rescue her before [[Nynaeve]] and [[Elayne]] did so.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=10m02s|text=10:02}} The [[Heroes of the Horn]] fought more or less on the ''same'' side as the [[Whitecloaks]] at [[Falme]]. They certainly didn't destroy them. It was the [[Seanchan]] (namely, the ''[[damane]]'') that destroyed the Whitecloaks, not the Heroes.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=10m25s|text=10:25}} Elaboration: an uninitiated viewer may be confused by the wording, but the "injury" they're referring to is a stab wound in [[Rand|Rand's]] side from [[Ba'alzamon|Ba'alzamon's]] blade; they're not redundantly referring to the heron brand again.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=11m06s|text=11:06}} [[Rand|Rand's]] outburst with the [[One Power]] could certainly be considered a ''result'' of his arguments with [[Moiraine]], but it was not during an argument. It occurred in the midst of a conversation with [[Perrin]], without Moiraine (nor anyone else) anywhere in sight.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=11m24s|text=11:24}} Rand did not "believe" "he caused the deaths of all who traveled with him." If this means he thought he killed [[Moiraine]], [[Min]], [[Perrin]], etc. that's simply not true. If it means that he left them so they wouldn't be in danger by being with him, that is not established in the text even if one can't categorically state that it's outright false (though it is certainly consistent with his character).
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=11m44s|text=11:44}} [[Masema]] did not go off on his own of his own initiative. In fact, [[Moiraine]] sent all the [[Shienar|Shienarans]] away. Masema only began his "ministry" after they discovered Moiraine's contact was deceased and they were left without clear direction. The idea that the presence of wolves in the fight in the mountains was the reason for Masema deciding to become the [[Prophet]] is laughably false. Masema was already a fanatic. Seeing the wolves was just one relatively inconsequential confirmation of his fanatic beliefs.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=11m58s|text=11:58}} None of the [[Shienar|Shienarans]] left the mountain camp with [[Moiraine]], [[Lan]], [[Perrin]], and [[Loial]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=12m13s|text=12:13}} [[Gaul]] stated he was looking for [[He Who Comes With the Dawn]], but he was not heading towards [[Tear]] until [[Perrin]] informed him that "He Who Comes WIth the Dawn" was heading there.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=13m38s|text=13:38}} There was never any direct indication that [[Mat|Mat's]] [[Old Tongue]] outburst had anything to do with a previous life. Rather, it is attributed to the "[[Old Blood]]" "running strong" in the [[Two Rivers]] in general and Mat in particular. In other words, it's credited to his ancestry, not his former lives, whatever they may have been. Aside from [[Rand]], the [[Heroes of the Horn]], and arguably [[Ishamael]], there is never any reference to any particular previous lives of any particular characters. The idea that they concluded Mat was [[Aemon al Caar al Thorin|Aemon]] reborn is complete nonsense. No statement in any of the books comes close to this.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=14m07s|text=14:07}} [[Thom]] was being a drunk, but he was not "wandering around"; he was performing in an inn.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=14m22s|text=14:22}} There is no indication whatsoever that [[Tammuz]] and his cronies were [[Darkfriends]]. In fact, [[Rand|Rand's]] misadventures in the [[Cairhien|Cairhienin]] [[Guild of Illuminators|chapter house]] could be considered slight evidence that Tammuz is ''not'' a Darkfriend. [[Mat]] and [[Thom]] were attacked by Darkfriends (twice) en route to [[Caemlyn]], but neither of these occurred in [[Aringill]] (though the attack on [[Aludra]] did). Also, technically Aludra no longer "belonged" to the Illuminators at this point.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=14m31s|text=14:31}} While [[Mat]] discovering the scale of the destructive power of fireworks as an explosive was certainly accidental, it's shortchanging Mat a bit to say that he discovered "how they work" by accident. He learned a fair bit by (sloppy) experimentation, and fully expected them to explode when they did - he simply didn't expect the power to be sufficient to actually do damage to the [[Stone of Tear|Stone]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=15m02s|text=15:02}} The animation has Mat going in the wrong direction. He should be returning southeast to [[Aringill]] en route to [[Tear]], not heading southwest towards [[Murandy]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=15m25s|text=15:25}} [[Mat]] met several [[Aiel]], not just [[Gaul]] and [[Rhuarc]]. Moreover, it is never established that Gaul leads the [[Stone Dogs]]. He might; that would explain why he in particular is with Rhuarc, but it is never established that Gaul holds any particular rank and, aside from him telling Rhuarc "it's time," we never see him acting in any way like a commander or official leader throughout the series. He is instead depicted simply as a superlative warrior, albeit one whose [[Wise One]] thinks should go to [[Rhuidean]] to become [[clan chief]].{{verify}}
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=15m35s|text=15:35}} [[Mat]] met [[Juilin]] ''while'' meeting the [[Aiel]], not afterwards.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=15m51s|text=15:51}} The animation is misleading. Setting aside that [[Mat]] and [[Juilin]] were on top of a wall that ended at the side of the [[Stone of Tear|Stone]] (and were not on the ground as shown), Mat did ''not'' set off the fireworks sporadically in varying directions like he was performing a fireworks display. He packed them tightly into an arrowslit and inadvertently made them into a jerry-rigged breaching charge.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=16m13s|text=16:13}} The animation shows [[Rand]] holding a conventional sword (''[[Callandor]]'' is visible in the background). He would have been using a sword made of solid flame conjured with the [[One Power]],{{verify}} not a physical sword, since [[Tam al'Thor's sword]] was destroyed during Rand's duel with [[Ba'alzamon]] at [[Falme]]. Also, Tam's sword was not a longsword.

==Nitpicks==
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=2m50s|text=2:50}} The wording of the first couple minutes makes it seem like [[Mat]] and [[Perrin|Perrin's]] estrangement from Rand occurred over the course of their time at Fal Dara, but it didn't really start until the last day or so. Also, the [[Shienar|Shienarans]] thought Rand was a lord/prince, not a king.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=2m57s|text=2:57}} It's ''the'' [[Two Rivers]], much like "the Gambia" or "the Amazon." One would never say "In Two Rivers, blah blah blah." Also, just to add to the statement about 'al', it technically meant 'son of' but that's an archaic meaning and the Two Rivers folk don't actually think of it that way. To them, it's just a common prefix at the beginning of surnames, in much the same way that 'son' is a common suffix to modern surnames (as in 'Johnson', 'Peterson', etc.) but doesn't truly mean 'son of' anymore.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=3m01s|text=3:01}} An English nitpick unrelated to WoT lore:  "One Nynaeve" is very strange wording. English speakers only say "one <Person>" when the person in question is unfamiliar to the speaker/writer/reader/listener. It's really odd to use that phrasing when referring to a character that's already been mentioned many times in this video series.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=3m25s|text=3:25}} "Sorceress" is not a term anyone would use in-universe. And there is no "Bronze" Ajah. [[Verin]] is [[Brown Ajah]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=5m32s|text=5:32}} "[[Ogier]] explained" implies the presence of multiple Ogier. To merely describe [[Loial]] explaining something, you'd say "the Ogier explained."
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=5m43s|text=5:43}} [[Rand]] thinks he's the one who transported them to the [[Portal Stone]] world, but imho it's far more likely that [[Lanfear]] did so.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=5m50s|text=5:50}} It's [[Artur Hawkwing]], not 'Arthur.'
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=6m42s|text=6:42}} "King [[Cairhien]]" is not how anyone in-universe would refer to [[Galldrian]]. He'd be called the "King of Cairhien."
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=6m51s|text=6:51}} While it's technically true that [[Galldrian]] and [[Barthanes]] were trying to get the "[[Dragon Reborn|Dragon Reborn's]]" attention, this is a very misleading phrasing, because no one in [[Cairhien]] except [[Fain]] (and [[Verin]] and [[Selene]] when they were present) knew that [[Rand]] was the Dragon Reborn. Even Rand didn't ''know'', as he was still in denial. [[Mat]] and [[Perrin]] similarly did not believe yet, and no one else except maybe [[Thom]] even suspected. At this point, Galldrian and Barthanes were simply trying to meet this man who to them was an enigmatic [[Andor|Andoran]] lord.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=6m56s|text=6:56}} I suppose the fireworks complex was indeed an "illustrious" chapter house, but given that the captions correct this to "[[Guild of Illuminators|Illuminator's]]" I'm guessing this wording was an accidental mistake.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=7m42s|text=7:42}} "Being [[Darkfriend]] himself" is grammatically incorrect. It should be "being '''''a''''' Darkfriend himself".
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=7m50s|text=7:50}} [[User blog:Androlf/W&W 5: The Dragon Reborn Returns|Again]], "the Roads" is not some alternate name for the [[Ways]]. They are only ever called the Ways.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=8m50s|text=8:50}} The phrasing here is a bit confusing and kind of implies that [[Turak Aladon]] and the [[Seanchan]] were long-time rulers of [[Falme]] rather than recent conquerors.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=10m35s|text=10:35}} There is technically scant evidence [[Rand]] did declare ''himself'' the Dragon Reborn at [[Falme]]. The [[Shienar|Shienarans]] and others certainly named him so after witnessing him duel [[Ba'alzamon]] in the sky above Falme. The final sentence of [[The Great Hunt/Chapter 49|Chapter 49]] of ''[[The Great Hunt]]'' simply says "He made his decision." This might imply he proclaimed himself, but the early chapters of ''[[The Dragon Reborn]]'' are somewhat inconsistent with this, using phrases along the lines of "he allowed them to proclaim him" and such in Rand's POVs.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=11m05s|text=11:05}} Again, one can't simply refer to [[Moiraine]] as "[[Blue Ajah]]." This wording implies that [[Rand]] is having disputes with the entire Blue Ajah, rather than a single member thereof.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=11m39s|text=11:39}} "Follow his lead" implies a degree of agreement or cooperation that certainly did not exist between [[Rand]] and [[Moiraine]] at this point. It would be more accurate to say that Moiraine decided to follow him.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=12m03s|text=12:03}} [[Moiraine|Moiraine's]] party found "an [[Aiel]]," they did not "find Aiel." As worded, it implies there were other Aiel caged with [[Gaul]] in [[Remen]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=14m14s|text=14:14}} As the captions reference, [[Mat]] was delivering the letter at [[Elayne|Elayne's]] request. As it stands, the video seems to imply he just decided to give a letter to [[Morgase]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/hWSCzS0ogcQ?t=16m20s|text=16:20}} It is never established that [[Lews Therin]] ever wielded ''[[Callandor]]''.{{verify}} Given what we know of Lews Therin and ''Callandor'', it seems likely he would have eschewed it if he had access to the ''[[Sakarnen]]'', or even a lesser ''sa'angreal''. That said, it is completely plausible that Lews Therin did use ''Callandor''.
